newsitem.title: USA: Iowa farmers prepare for corn and soybean planting.
newsitem.headline: Iowa farmers prepare for corn and soybean planting.

text.p: Iowa farmers applied fertilizers and prepared seedbeds for planting in the week ended April 6, the state's Iowa Agricultural Statistics Service said in the year's first weekly report.

Very warm temperatures during the week allowed many farmers into the field. Application of anhydrous ammonia seemed to be the most common activity. Farmers were 47 percent complete applying fertilizer.
"A cold, wet and windy storm over the weekend virtually stopped field work and left farmers waiting for the 'real' onset of spring," the report said.

Soil moisture was rated one percent very short, nine percent short, 76 percent adequate and 14 percent surplus. Frost was reported up to one foot deep in many areas in the northern two-thirds of the state.
Oats were 27 percent planted, slightly ahead of the five-year average of 26 percent.

Winter wheat was rated one percent very poor, two percent poor, 21 percent fair, 64 percent good and 12 percent excellent. As of Friday, reporters said they expected about three percent of the winter wheat acreage will be lost due to winter kill.
